A 16-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a 1-month history of fever, headaches, and profound fatigue. Her temperature is 38.2°C (100.8°F). Examination shows splenomegaly. Laboratory studies show:
Leukocyte count 13,000/mm3 (15% atypical lymphocytes)
Serum
Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 60 U/L
Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 40 U/L
Heterophile antibody assay negative
EBV viral capsid antigen (VCA) antibodies negative
HIV antibody negative
In an immunocompromised host, the causal organism of this patient's symptoms would most likely cause which of the following conditions?"?

                    ### Question
                    A 16-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a 1-month history of fever, headaches, and profound fatigue. Her temperature is 38.2°C (100.8°F). Examination shows splenomegaly. Laboratory studies show:
Leukocyte count 13,000/mm3 (15% atypical lymphocytes)
Serum
Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 60 U/L
Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) 40 U/L
Heterophile antibody assay negative
EBV viral capsid antigen (VCA) antibodies negative
HIV antibody negative
In an immunocompromised host, the causal organism of this patient's symptoms would most likely cause which of the following conditions?"?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Multiple cerebral abscesses with surrounding edema
opb. Diffuse pulmonary infiltrates with pneumatoceles
opc. Purplish skin nodules on the distal extremities
opd. Non-scrapable white patches on the lateral tongue
ope. Linear ulcers near the lower esophageal sphincter

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The 16-year-old girl presents with fever, splenomegaly, and elevated liver enzymes, suggesting a viral infection. The negative heterophile antibody assay and EBV VCA antibodies indicate that infectious mononucleosis due to EBV is unlikely. In an immunocompromised host, Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is a common opportunistic infection. CMV can cause various complications, including linear ulcers near the lower esophageal sphincter, diffuse pulmonary infiltrates with pneumatoceles, and multiple cerebral abscesses. However, CMV does not typically cause purplish skin nodules or non-scrapable white patches on the tongue. Therefore, the most likely condition caused by CMV in this context is linear ulcers near the lower esophageal sphincter, supported by the patient's immunocompromised state and the known complications of CMV infection.
